counterexamples.why: Two `in` guards over different value lists are independently true or false of one component, so all four combinations are realisable; `n + 1` counts three.
An object can carry both named keys, either one, or neither, so a pair of `containsKey` guards realises four signatures rather than three.

invalidated.large_values_were_clamped: `p99_cells` for IAM is the 10^9 cap published verbatim, not a measurement; the instrument now keeps the exact integer and reports `exceeds_enumeration_limit` separately.
invalidated.reinstating_requires: Re-running with --replace-invalidated, and restoring the claims struck from docs/REPRODUCING_THE_STUDY.md and scripts/check_manuscript.py in the same change.
invalidated.same_defect_in_iam: `iam_guards` recorded one guard per (operator, condition key) while an AWS condition value is an array, so `StringEquals` against a multi-entry array was counted as a single-value guard for the same invalid reason.
invalidated.summary: The distribution below is withdrawn. It was computed with a guard grouping that counted set-membership operators as holding of at most one value each, so on any component carrying two of them the count is an under-estimate -- the one direction a 'this many policies need at most this many cases' claim cannot survive.
